## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). 4-bets and 3-bets extremely wide. **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything — including calling multi-street donk-leads with just overcards. C-bets most flops, checks dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); MEDIUM HANDS → checks turn, calls river (station mode); REAL HANDS → shoves aggressively. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **As NON-PFA (BB defend, etc.)**: Fit-or-fold — folds to c-bets when whiffing. **DONK-LEADS with strong made hands (especially in 3-bet pots).** **CHECK-RAISES with semi-bluffs/draws on wet boards** — barrels turn with equity, CHECK-FOLDS river when draw misses. **Key line: P2 check-raise flop → bet turn → check river = BUSTED DRAW — attack with river bet.** Calls 3-bets with pocket pairs (including JJ) rather than 4-betting. **Exploit**: Flat opens IP with suited broadways/connectors. 3-bet QQ+/AKs only. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. DO NOT bluff when P2 is calling with made hands. DO bluff when P2's line = busted draw. **As 3-bet caller: c-bet when P2 checks (will fold air); FOLD to P2's donk-lead + turn aggression (strong).** Finished last — bleeds chips to exploitative play.

**Player 3**: **Tight-aggressive, skilled — most dangerous opponent (~7% VPIP).** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium. 3-bets from blinds vs ALL positions. **Confirmed trapper — wide check-raise range** on wet boards in 3-bet pots. C-betting is SELECTIVE. Triple-barrels one-pair value. Floating P3 is LOW EV. **Doesn't bluff-catch wide vs multi-street aggression** — calls flop+turn then folds river to escalating bets. **Exploit**: Stab when P3 checks back. Multi-street barrels work — call flop+turn, fold river to size. Don't value-bet thin on river. Call 3-bets IP with strong suited hands only. Good steal target in blinds (folds to LP opens).

**Player 4**: **Tight (~13% VPIP), passive preflop, MIXED postflop. EXTREME calling station.** Calls 3-bets with junk. Calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. PASSIVE with strong made hands — checks made straights through ALL streets. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+). 5-BET SHOVE includes JJ.** As single-raiser: C-bets flop, folds to turn raises — FLOATABLE. **As LIMPER: DOUBLE-BARRELS aggressively with draws (OESD), then GIVES UP on river when draw misses.** P4 limp → lead-lead-check = often BUSTED DRAW (river bet may work despite general stickiness). **Exploit**: 3-bet for VALUE only. Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target). NEVER bluff P4 when calling (sticky). Respect check-raises/donk-bets/limp-reraises/3-bets. Targetable in blinds.

**Player 5**: **Very tight nit (~7% VPIP), sticky with pocket pairs.** C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. Donk-bets can be strong OR weak — weak ones fold to raises/turn barrels; strong ones ESCALATE. **ANY turn raise from P5 = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Call flop c-bets wider. FOLD to P5's turn raises always. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wide limper, opener, AND cold-caller. More competent than raw classification suggests (finished 2nd).** **As LIMPER: EXTREMELY sticky postflop — calls with bottom pair. BUT folds preflop to large iso-raises, especially vs tight image.** **As COLD-CALLER: Donk-leads with AIR/weak draws → RAISE for fold equity. CHECK-CALLS with real made hands (top pair weak kicker) — passive line = actual hand.** Key tell: P6 donk-lead = air; P6 check-call = real hand. MASSIVE overbets = value. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED.** As PFA: Folds to turn donk-leads on DRY boards only; calls on wet boards. **Exploit**: Value bet wide. Isolate limps — SIZE DOWN iso-raises (~3x) to keep P6 in. NEVER bluff when P6 is sticky/check-calling. RAISE donk-leads (they're air). FOLD to 4-bet shoves/overbets. Note: P6 accumulates chips — may be better hand-reader than appears.

**Player 7**: **Wide opener AND wide blind defender, passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop. SLOW-PLAYS PREMIUMS preflop (cold-called 5-bet all-in with QQ).** Donk-leads and triple-barrels with strength. Checks down with air. **Exploit**: Value-bet relentlessly, size up. Beware cold-call/limp traps. Don't bluff.

## Self-Assessment & Table Image

**Image entering next session: VERY LOOSE-AGGRESSIVE.** ~50% VPIP in early session, multiple shown bluffs, Q3s at showdown. Finished as chip leader ($1457).
- Won chip lead primarily through TARGETED AGGRESSION — 7 of 9 wins were "last player standing" (opponents folding)
- Biggest loss was -$260 with KQ — **KQ is a TROUBLE HAND at this table** (lost significant pot). Be cautious with KQ facing heavy action.
- Loose image = thin value MORE profitable, bluff credibility LOW
- **Image recalibration is #1 PRIORITY** — tighten to 25-30% VPIP in early session, show down strong hands to rebuild fold equity before resuming aggression

## Core Strategy for Next Session

1. **TIGHTEN UP early** (25-30% VPIP). Show strong showdowns to rebuild credibility. Then gradually reintroduce selective aggression.
2. **Thin value > bluffing** against stations (P2, P4, P6, P7). Loose image makes value even more profitable.
3. **Bluffing is LINE-BASED only.** Target specific opponent patterns: P2's busted draw line (CR→barrel→check); P4's lead-lead-check; weak P6 donk-leads.
4. **SIZE DOWN iso-raises vs P6** (~3x) to keep them calling with dominated hands.
5. **Float P2 and P5 on flops** — both shut down on turn without hands.
6. **Multi-street barrels work vs P3** — calls two streets, folds river to escalation.
7. **Never bluff P4 (calling station), P6 (when check-calling), P7 (aggressive with strength).**
8. **Blind steals still viable vs P3/P4/P5** but expect wider defense given my image.
9. **Be cautious with KQ** — don't overcommit without strong board connection.

**Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P7 (aggressive/trappy) > P6 (underestimated competence) > P2 (LAG volume) > P5 (tight/predictable). P4 dangerous when aggressive (respect 3-bets/check-raises).
